errors.english: this relates to the object of perception
errors.why: The Tibetan says the phrase is construed with the verb 'is perceived' (dmigs), not that it refers to an object of perception.

errors.english: The phrase "at that time" should be placed first
errors.why: What is placed first is 'that cause' (rgyu de), supplied from the relative 'which'; 'at that time' is only the lemma being explained.

errors.english: Even if any particular humor like wind were the cause, not every particular instance would possess all forms of desire and so forth. One must infer this by observing the certain result at all times.
errors.why: The whole passage from 'gal te rlung...' is the anticipated objection introduced by 'But if the result', not the author's own assertion.

note: Generally follows the commentary, but several construal glosses are misread and an objection is partly presented as the author's view.

errors.english: it is not the case that they are excluded from being reasons themselves
errors.why: The Tibetan says they are not separated out (as an exception) to become reasons; the English implies they are reasons.

note: A sound rendering of a difficult dialectical passage, with verses kept as verse; one sentence inverts the point.

errors.english: refers to the position of we
errors.why: pha rol gyi means the passage is the opponent's statement, not 'our' position.

fix.find: refers to the position of we

errors.english: such as arising and not arising
errors.why: The pair paralleling 'mind and mental factors' is the elements and what is derived from them (bhūta/bhautika), not arising and non-arising.

errors.english: between feelings like pleasure and other sentient factors
errors.why: sems pa can here is the Sāṃkhya conscious principle (cetana/puruṣa), contrasted with pleasure etc. (the guṇas), not 'other sentient factors'.

note: Readable, but Sāṃkhya terminology is misread and the opponent's statement is attributed to the author's side.

errors.english: if one speaks without error regarding fire
errors.why: mi 'khrul ba is the logical non-deviation of smoke from fire (avyabhicāra), not speaking without error.

fix.find: if one speaks without error regarding fire
fix.replace: if one states that smoke never deviates from fire

errors.english: here referring to a specific plant or substance named after him
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan in this stock example is an anthill emitting smoke-like vapour, not a plant or substance.

fix.find: here referring to a specific plant or substance named after him
fix.replace: śakramūrdhan, the anthill from which smoke-like vapour rises

note: The argument is mostly followed, but the key logical term 'non-deviation' is mistranslated and the stock example is wrongly glossed.

errors.english: if the person being carried is standing on land included within the border but has no such purpose [note: of evasion], there is no downfall
errors.why: khyer ba po is the carrier, and the rule is: where (the magic) needs no carrier standing on land within the boundary there is no offence, but where there is such a carrier it is a sthūlātyaya. The English makes it the carried person's intention.

note: Generally adequate on a technical Vinaya passage, but the final rule on carriers is misconstrued.

errors.english: The sapphire and the peacock's crest are both praised for their precious quality.
errors.why: The verse says that although the blue is the same in sapphire and peacock eye-feather, it is praised only where it resides in the jewel.

fix.find: The sapphire and the peacock's crest are both praised for their precious quality.
fix.replace: In the sapphire and the peacock's eye-feather, it is praised where it resides in the jewel.

errors.english: with the permission of Chandra, the lord of men, the brothers went to their own lands
errors.why: Candra, with the permission of the lord of men (the king), went with his brothers to his own land; Candra does not grant the permission.

errors.english: Having developed noble qualities and a fine intellect, he became a most venerable object of praise.
errors.why: This is the first line of the stanza, a general maxim about one born with virtues, and it has been turned into narrative prose about Candra.
'From us' is not in the Tibetan; Candra is to be separated from what is charming (or his life), not from the speakers.

note: The narrative is followed, but the gnomic verses are partly misread and the permission is misattributed.

errors.english: a collection of seeds or the seeds of an abode of living beings
errors.why: The list of objects includes sprouted shoots (khye'u kha 'thon pa), which the English leaves out.

note: A faithful rendering of the Vinaya definitions; the plant and insect names are reasonably handled.

errors.english: when the pillars do not support [the load]
errors.why: The example is lifting a beam (gdung ma 'degs pa): people who cannot lift it individually can when combined; it is not about pillars failing to support.

fix.find: when the pillars do not support [the load], those

note: Sound on the argument about the whole and its parts, apart from the misread beam-lifting example.

errors.english: the property of the thesis being a part of it
errors.why: This is the definition 'pakṣadharma [pervaded] by a part of it (tadaṃśena)'; the English makes the property itself a part.

note: Follows the dense logic in a literal but often opaque way, and misreads the key definitional phrase.

errors.english: the meaning of the (Sutra) scriptural discourse
errors.why: mdo here is the root text (the verse) being commented on, not a scriptural discourse of the Buddha.

fix.find: the meaning of the (Sutra) scriptural discourse
fix.replace: the meaning of the root text

errors.english: if one were to search for them atom by atom
errors.why: The argument is that when the atoms are removed one by one, the cognition of a pot no longer arises; it is not about searching.

note: A good rendering of the atom argument, with one mislabelled root text and one blurred example.
